question.text:
Let f : A → B and g : B → A satisfy g ◦ f = id . Which must be true?
A
(A) f and g are bijective
(B) f is surjective and g is injective
(C) f is injective and g is surjective
(D) g ◦ f = f ◦ g
(E) A = B

solution.text:

If f(a) = f(a ), applying g gives a = a , so f is injective. Every a ∈ A equals g(f(a)), so g
is onto. Inclusion of a one-element set into a two-element set with a left inverse shows the
other two properties need not hold.
